observations.why: The collective 'we' enacts a decisional posture that binds the group — a communal we-ness performing an authoritative adoption, but the relational move is the collective decision itself, not undifferentiated sharing.
Performance is framed as a proportional cost-benefit comparison — a quantitative ratio justifying the choice on proportionality grounds.
A timeline is set for the collective — the speaker commits the group to a scheduled action, enacting authority over when the organization moves.
The summary re-presents the proportional performance gain as the organizing rationale — market-pricing proportionality is the frame that consolidates the decision.
